summary.plain: The CAST detector reused a retired magnet originally built for the Large Hadron Collider, pointed it at the Sun, and looked for the faint X-rays that would appear if hypothetical axion particles convert into light inside the magnet.
summary.technical: Straight, twin-bore prototype LHC dipole magnet (formerly LEP DELPHI cryogenics) tracking the Sun, coupled to X-ray optics and detectors for the axion helioscope technique; data-taking 2003-06-18 to 2022-12-31.

technology.value: Axion helioscope: a decommissioned LHC prototype superconducting dipole magnet, pointed at the Sun, with its hollow beam-pipe bores acting as viewing tubes for X-ray optics and X-ray detectors that look for photons produced by solar axions converting in the magnetic field.
